verses.text: The apostles and the believers throughout Judea heard that Gentiles had also accepted God’s word.
When Peter came up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers challenged him.
They said, “You went into the home of uncircumcised men and ate with them!”
So Peter began explaining the whole story to them in order:
“I was praying in Joppa and fell into a trance. I saw a vision of something like a large sheet lowered from heaven by its four corners. It came right down to me.
“I looked closely and saw four-legged animals, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
“Then I heard a voice say, ‘Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.’
“I replied, ‘No, Lord. Nothing impure or unclean has ever gone into my mouth.’
“The voice from heaven answered a second time, ‘Don’t call unclean what God has made clean.’
“This happened three times, and then everything was taken back up into heaven.
“At that very moment, three men sent from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
“The Spirit told me to go with them without hesitation. These six brothers came with me too, and we entered the man’s house.
“He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said, ‘Send to Joppa and bring Simon, also called Peter.
“‘He will tell you a message through which you and your whole household will be saved.’
“As I began speaking, the Holy Spirit came upon them just as he came upon us at the beginning.
“Then I remembered what the Lord had said: ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
“If God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to stand in God’s way?”
When they heard this, they stopped objecting and praised God. They said, “So God has also given Gentiles the opportunity to turn to him and receive life!”
The believers scattered by the persecution that began around Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They shared the message only with Jews.
But some believers from Cyprus and Cyrene went to Antioch and began telling Greek-speaking people the Good News about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord’s power was with them, and a large number believed and turned to the Lord.
News about them reached the church in Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When he arrived and saw God’s grace at work, he was glad. He encouraged them all to stay true to the Lord with firm commitment.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many more people came to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul.
When he found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they met with the church and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.
During that time, some prophets came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up and announced through the Spirit that a severe famine would spread across the whole world. It happened during Claudius’s reign.
So the disciples decided that each would send help to the believers living in Judea, as much as they were able.
They sent the relief to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.
